additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is defined by recurrent binge-eating episodes involving objectively large amounts of food with a felt loss of control, accompanied by features such as rapid eating, eating when not physically hungry, and marked guilt or disgust afterward. It typically has a fluctuating course over months to years and is distinguished from bulimia nervosa by the absence of regular compensatory behaviors such as purging, fasting, or excessive exercise.

patient.stressor_event: Changing to a different line of work
patient.stressor: When Fumi began trying to move from commercial cleaning into design work, she kept her cleaning shifts while taking on unpaid portfolio projects and late-night sketching deadlines, leaving her days unstructured and her meals irregular. Over the next 1 year and 2 months, what began as occasional midnight ramen or convenience-store stops after work gradually became discrete periods of eating much more than she intended, often quickly and even when she was not physically hungry, with a growing sense that she could not stop once she started. Because she was still getting to work and attending art events, the problem stayed private, but her journal entries became increasingly filled with disgust and guilt after these episodes. She finally brought it up during a student-health counseling intake arranged through a community design program, saying she was worried her eating had become something she could no longer manage by willpower alone.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On some nights after my cleaning shift, I’ll stop at the convenience store and end up eating a big bowl of ramen, several rice balls, fried chicken, and sweets in my room within an hour or two, even though I only meant to grab dinner.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically, and even while I’m thinking, 'Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,' I don’t actually stop until the food is gone or I feel too uncomfortable.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat really fast during those times, standing at the counter or sitting on my bed with my sketchbook still open, barely tasting anything and just trying to get it down before I can think too much.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: A lot of the time I’m not even hungry, like I might have already eaten after work, but if I’m tired or stuck on a design idea I still start opening snacks and keep going.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: I came in because after these eating episodes I feel so gross and disappointed in myself, like I should have more control, and I end up writing awful things about myself in my journal.

add_requirements.binge_eating_at_least_weekly_for_3_month: For the past several months, there has usually been at least one night each week where I buy too much food after work and eat it all in one stretch. I can’t remember a recent month where it stopped for more than a week or so.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I still make it to my cleaning shifts and design events, but the next day I feel distracted and ashamed, and sometimes I put off sketching because I don’t want to look at the journal entries I wrote afterward.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about 1 year and 2 months, since I started trying to switch from cleaning work into design while keeping my old shifts.
